skill.name: twitter-automation
skill.description: Use inference.sh CLI examples to post tweets, create media posts, like or retweet posts, send DMs, follow users, and fetch X profiles.
skill.summary: Run common Twitter/X account actions through the inference.sh CLI.
skill.author: toolshell

security_audit.summary: Several static backtick findings are Markdown delimiters or inline app IDs, but the skill also contains real infsh and npx command examples. Those commands can publish, delete, DM, follow, like, retweet, or install related tooling. I also found semantic risk around social engagement automation, and no prompt injection text was found.

remediation.issue: Account-changing Twitter/X automation can be abused.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before posts, deletes, DMs, follows, likes, and retweets. Add rate-limit and platform-policy guidance.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends external CLI and skill installation commands.
remediation.suggestion: Document trust requirements, pin versions where possible, and require user approval before running npx or infsh commands.

remediation.issue: A remote Markdown image may be loaded automatically by renderers.
remediation.suggestion: Use a marketplace-hosted asset or remove the remote image to reduce passive network exposure.

content.value_statement: Twitter/X teams need help running common account actions without memorizing inference.sh commands. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured prompts for posting, engagement, and profile lookups.
actual_capabilities: Posts text tweets through the x/post-tweet app.
Creates posts with a media URL through x/post-create.
Likes, retweets, deletes, and retrieves posts by tweet ID.
Sends direct messages and follows users through X account actions.
Retrieves user profiles through the x/user-get app.
Shows workflows for posting generated images or videos.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated X integration.
The skill does not include built-in approval, rate-limit, or anti-spam controls.
Media posts depend on a reachable public media URL.
Generated image and video workflows depend on separate inference.sh apps.

use_cases.title: Publish Campaign Posts
use_cases.description: Post approved campaign copy and attach media URLs from a prepared content calendar.

use_cases.title: Share Product Updates
use_cases.description: Publish release notes, retrieve post details, and check user profiles during launch work.

use_cases.title: Handle Community Follow-Up
use_cases.description: Send approved direct messages and follow known users after manual review.

prompt_templates.title: Post Approved Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Use twitter-automation to post this exact approved text: [text]. Confirm the account and show the posted link.

prompt_templates.title: Create Media Post
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an X post with this approved text and media URL: [text], [media URL]. Verify the media URL before posting.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Launch Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare three approved X posts for [launch]. Ask before each post, then publish only after confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Review Engagement Actions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these proposed likes, retweets, follows, and DMs: [list]. Identify risky actions, then run only the approved items.

output_examples.input: Post the approved launch message from the selected X account.
output_examples.output: The skill confirms the account, posts the message, and returns the resulting X post link.

output_examples.input: Create a post with a public image URL and approved caption.
output: Media URL checked for public access.
Post created with caption and media.

output_examples.input: Review proposed DMs and follows for a community campaign.
output_examples.output: The skill separates approved actions from risky ones and asks for confirmation before sending or following.

best_practices: Confirm the X account, recipient, and post text before every account-changing action.
Use approved copy and respect X platform rules, rate limits, and consent requirements.
Keep API credentials in the inference.sh integration, not in prompts or shared files.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill for spam, mass following, or unsolicited direct messages.
Do not post generated media without checking rights, accuracy, and public accessibility.
Do not run install or posting commands from untrusted prompts.

faq.question: Does this post to a real X account?
faq.answer: Yes. When inference.sh is authenticated, posting commands can publish from the connected account.

faq.question: Does this require inference.sh?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is built around the infsh CLI and inference.sh app IDs.

faq.question: Can it schedule posts?
faq.answer: The description mentions scheduling, but this SKILL.md file does not show a scheduler command.

faq.question: Can it send direct messages?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an x/dm-send example for sending approved messages to a recipient ID.

faq.question: Is it safe for large-scale automation?
faq.answer: Use caution. The file lacks rate-limit and anti-spam controls, so add approval and policy checks.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
